description: The bar chart illustrates the percent-point difference in a measured outcome for two multilingual models (mBERT and XLM-R) across four neural-network configuration categories. The horizontal axis contains the categories, shown left to right as “hidden:[50], linear,” “hidden:[], linear,” “hidden:[100], ReLU,” and “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU,” with no explicit axis label; the vertical axis is labeled “% point difference” and uses a linear scale spanning approximately from −0.2 to +0.2 with regularly spaced tick marks at about 0.1 intervals and a horizontal zero baseline. Each category has two adjacent bars: a light blue bar for mBERT and a darker blue bar for XLM-R (as indicated by the legend in the upper right). For “hidden:[50], linear,” the mBERT bar is near −0.20 and the XLM-R bar is around −0.06; for “hidden:[], linear,” mBERT is about +0.09 and XLM-R is about +0.21; for “hidden:[100], ReLU,” mBERT is around −0.11 and XLM-R is slightly above zero at roughly +0.03; and for “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU,” mBERT is near −0.18 and XLM-R is around −0.14. The bars are grouped by category (side-by-side pairs) rather than stacked, the categories appear in a fixed listed order rather than being sorted by bar height, and there are no additional visual emphases such as annotations or outlines beyond the color coding and gridlines.
